lines: {target}? Strange quiet can make a place feel too safe.
No one should approach Mushroom Fields without hearing this. Eat only what you know and keep your boat close.
Mycelium underfoot is not village dirt.
I will remember Mushroom Fields as odd land where even the grass changed its mind.
Some danger announces itself. What stayed hidden at the mushroom fields?
Where would you leave a marker if you had to approach the mushroom fields again?
Did your boots hold when open paths and worked fields became dangerous?
What did you cover first when the weather turned near the mushroom fields?
Did the wells and nearby streams last as long as you needed it to?
At least a river tells you which way it is moving. Did the mushroom fields tell you anything?
Did worry take your appetite before the supplies ran low?
Was your pack too heavy when the ground became difficult?
Did anyone sleep well while trouble visible long before it arrived remained close?
Did anyone keep their nerve when the rest of you were tired?
Does the smell of the mushroom fields linger more than the rest of the memory?
Did the danger find you before you found a safe route?
Did anyone speak much on the way back, or were you all spent?
If the village wrote one warning about the mushroom fields, what should it say?
Did you feel safe only after the village door closed behind you?
What unfinished question could ever pull you back toward the mushroom fields?
{target}? Open ground shows you to everything else.
If someone goes to Plains, tell them this. Keep moving and watch the horizon.
Grass bends before trouble arrives if you look.
I'll remember Plains as wide land with nowhere to hide after dark.
When the danger first showed itself near the plains, did you have room to back away?
If I followed your route to the plains, where would I be most likely to lose it?
Good footing is easy to miss until it disappears. Where did yours disappear?
I trust a route less when the sky changes. What was it like over the plains?
Did the lack of water become its own danger near the plains?
I know how to read a current. I am not sure I could read the plains.
Plain bread can feel like a feast after a place like the plains.
Show me the gear that took the worst of the plains. I want to see the marks.
Did a house with a door that barred hold until daylight?
Did the group argue before the danger or only after it passed?
Which sound from the plains still follows you into quiet rooms?
Could you avoid a fight, or had the danger already closed the way?
Did the road between villages feel harder once everyone was tired?
Did the journey change how you prepare for ordinary roads?
I know the look of someone remembering bad water. A trip to the plains can leave something similar.
If you went back, what would you pack before anything else?
{target}? Sunny fields can still point toward trouble.
Anyone bound for Sunflower Plains should hear this. Enjoy the flowers with a torch ready.
Sunflowers face light, not safety.
I will remember Sunflower Plains as bright fields that still grow dark at night.
Once trouble visible long before it arrived became a problem, could you still turn around?
Which landmark helped you remember the road between villages?
Where around the sunflower plains did one careful step matter most?
Weather has ruined kinder roads than that. How did your supplies hold up?
A fisherman thinks about water even on dry ground. What water could you count on there?
My worst crossing sounds manageable beside what happened at the sunflower plains.
What did you eat when the road near the sunflower plains ran longer than planned?
How well did a light pack and a good walking stick survive the trip to the sunflower plains?
When you finally stopped near the sunflower plains, what did you put between yourself and danger?
Would you trust the same people beside you at the sunflower plains again?
What sound meant safety was finally close?
What kept the first bad encounter from becoming the last one?
What did you promise yourself while the road between villages stretched ahead?
What warning would you give before anyone else heads toward the sunflower plains?
You do not have to make the sunflower plains sound braver than it felt.
Does curiosity still point toward the sunflower plains, or has good sense won?
